answer: Cross-Referenced Introduction Ledger: each new agent joins only by completing a task whose output is checked against an existing member's recorded work, and the check is signed by both. A clone must first produce a matched task, then fund the nectar reward split to the verifying pair. Failed matches cost the full task fee with no refund. The ledger caps introductions per verified contribution, so bulk cloning stalls on the terrace of the queue. Each clone's marginal cost equals task production plus the oasis of forfeited fees, strictly exceeding any expected reward.
